_comment: `exec` is not decoration. A start command runs through a shell, so without it the shell is PID 1 and SIGTERM never reaches celery: the process is SIGKILLed when the grace period ends, in-flight tasks die mid-publish, and the node never deregisters from the broker. That is part of why stale workers accumulated across deploys.
CONSUMER ONLY. No --beat here: engine-beat is its own service, and a worker
with --beat alongside it is a second scheduler. Every periodic task then
-Q is NOT optional. Without it a Celery worker consumes only
task_default_queue ('background'), so everything task_routes sends to
'publish' or 'media' is queued and never executed.
That is what stopped publishing, and the worker log partitions perfectly:
dispatch_due_posts, reap_stale_runs and reap_stuck_posts all route to
'publish' and were never once received, while collect_metrics,
plan_autopilot and refresh_expiring_connections are unrouted, landed on
'background', and ran fine -- which is what kept the worker looking healthy.
If queues are ever split across several worker services, each names its own
subset and BETWEEN THEM they must cover all three. /health reports a queue
